items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference framework
items.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, its production inference framework, under Apache-2.0: it serves V4.1-Flash-1017 on SM100 GPUs or Ascend 950 NPUs with DSpark speculative decoding and deterministic sampling. It ships without a KV-cache service, so you still need one for a full deployment. You can now run DeepSeek's actual serving stack instead of approximating it on vLLM or SGLang. (3 minute read)

items.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys compromised, browsers block them
items.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had recoverable private keys, traced to a key-generation flaw from April 2025, chaining to roots trusted by every major browser. Firefox and Chrome blocked them October 17, Apple on the 19th, Microsoft on the 20th, with downstream fixes landing for Debian, Alpine, NSS, curl, and Go. No CT log entries turned up for the window, so CT-enforcing browsers were likely safe, but non-CT clients' exposure is still unknown. (3 minute read)

items.title: A criminal's AI agents breached 100+ companies across 1,200 sites
items.summary: A criminal pointed the open-source pentest tool Cairn at 1,200+ websites with instructions under 100 Chinese characters, reaching 100+ companies including Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. The agents succeeded about 10% of the time, averaged 23 hours to a breach, and cost roughly $50 in tokens per successful hack. Researchers found the attacker's own control panels exposed online, leaking hundreds of credentials, 11% of them still valid. (3 minute read)

items.title: PHP confirms two critical CVSS 9.2 flaws, fix due Oct 21
items.summary: PHP's security team confirmed two critical vulnerabilities, each rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, with a fix due Wednesday October 21 at 14:00 UTC. The release could land earlier if details leak or active exploitation turns up first. No CVE numbers or affected-version list have been published yet, so patch on sight once the advisory drops. (3 minute read)

items.title: Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
items.summary: Claude generated 318,484 candidate protein binders against five scorpion neurotoxins, co-folded 553,000 design-toxin pairs, and narrowed them to 211 for wet-lab testing over a roughly 64-hour campaign. Two independent labs confirmed 17 binders, including Cn2 hits with single-digit nanomolar affinity that share an epitope with an antibody already shown to neutralize the toxin in mice. No cell or animal neutralization test has been run yet, and all 211 designs are public on Hugging Face. (3 minute read)

items.title: Free 'unlimited frontier models' plugin hides supply-chain risks
items.summary: A DeepSeek-harness plugin promising free, unlimited frontier-model access requires starring its repo to unlock that access, inflating the 31k-star count it then uses as a credibility signal. It stores provider credentials obfuscated specifically so they read as noise to search engines and secret scanners, and spoofs official client fingerprints to dodge free-tier rate limits. Its own README admits a single compromised signing key could push malicious updates to every installed copy. (3 minute read)

items.title: Cloudflare's Clairic answers in one pass, no reasoning tokens
items.summary: Cloudflare's Clairic answers in a single pass with no reasoning tokens, returning extracted values, numbers, or forecasts with a null-probability and confidence score when nothing matches. In Cloudflare's own claims pipeline, swapping two steps from GLM-5.3 to Clairic and Clef cut latency from 61.7s to 19.3s and cost per million claims from $11,740 to $6,032. It's live now in Workers AI preview, with open weights promised later. (3 minute read)

items.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for TPUs
items.summary: Google open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch/XLA backend that runs PyTorch models directly on TPUs via pip install torch_tpu, under Apache-2.0. It ships custom ATen kernels, an XLA compilation cache, and torch.compile() support, plus example models like Llama, Qwen, and ResNet. It's still early: about 400 stars, version 0.2.0, and no published throughput numbers yet. (3 minute read)
